summary: A red steel pier light of 1906 at the mouth of the Milwaukee River; its keepers lived on a separate crib pier until the Coast Guard automated it in 1966.

access.note: Not open to public visitation (2012 nomination); on the north pier, reached from the southeast corner of Henry W. Maier Festival Park.

notes_for_editor: Chronology of 1872 to 1905 rests on LighthouseFriends (copyrighted; paraphrased), which quotes older Light-House Board reports not in the local corpus (corpus covers 1891 onward). The nomination and LighthouseFriends disagree on the 1872 tower and on when the rear range light went; both stated in text. LighthouseFriends says a fourth-order lens replaced the sixth in 1876, while USLHS event list says original lens fourth order. Foster's 1905 account: LighthouseFriends quotes it, newspaper confirms only the rescue. The July 1917 Dewey rescue year is taken from the 1917 Bulletin volume (item lacks a year line); the Commissioner's fiscal 1918 rescue list names the same keepers. Commissioner 1921 repair cost not tied to the 1917 storm by any source. Roster lines in the USLHS list were read from the tool output, not matched by column. Rear range 'discontinued 1926' vs 'early 1930s' are both in the nomination. Current ownership after the 2014 excess notice not established. Characteristic Fl R 4s from 2012/2004 sources; record says Fl G.
